summary: Tadashi Tani is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He completed doctoral studies at Waseda University (~1970–1977), did domestic study at Kyoto University (1995) under Yuichi Kajiyama, and served as professor at National Institute of Technology, Kochi College (~1988–2006).
Tadashi Toda is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Keiki Higashimoto and Kogen Mizuno.

Tadeusz Skorupski is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his Ph.D. from the University of London by 1978. He served at SOAS University of London as professor (attested 1987–1996) and reader (attested 2005).
Tai-shing Wut is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology who completed a PhD at The University of Hong Kong under doctoral supervisor Ming-Wood Liu.
Taido Kitamura is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who held posts at Shuchiin University, where he served as an assistant professor (attested 1980) and held an attested post in 1994–1999.

Taigen Dan Leighton is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who earned a BA from Columbia University and a Ph.D. from Graduate Theological Union. He taught as an adjunct professor at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (1994) and Loyola University Chicago (attested 2010).
Taijo Iwata is a scholar in Buddhist studies who served as a lecturer at Rissho University (attested 1984) and as a professor at Otani University (attested 1996).

Taijun Inokuchi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He served at Ryukoku University as a lecturer (attested 1963) and committee member (attested 1973–1987), and led the Society for the History of Buddhism (attested 1988).

Taiken Kimura (1881–1930) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo under Junjirō Takakusu and Tetsujiro Inoue, later serving at Tokyo as assistant professor (1912) and professor (1918–1930).
Taiken Kyuma works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Vienna by 1999 and served as an associate professor at Mie University (attested 2002–2008).
Taiken Tanaka is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied at Hiroshima University and served as an assistant professor at Aichi Gakuin University (attested 1991).
Taiki Mibu is a scholar in Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at Ryukoku University by 2016 and served there as a part-time lecturer (attested 2015).

Taikyo Tanigawa is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Koyasan University and earned a Ph.D. at Toyo University by 1994, later serving as assistant professor (attested 1980–1988) and professor (attested 2005) at Koyasan University.
Taion Satomi is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University until 1933 and served as a professor at Minobusan Junior College (attested 1972).

Taira Shidehara (1870–1953) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Sinology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1891–1894) and held posts at Tokyo University of Education (~1900–1906) and the University of Tokyo (~1906–1919).
Tairyu Tsunoda is a scholar in Buddhist studies who served as a lecturer at Komazawa Junior College (attested 1995) and became a professor at Komazawa University (attested 2015).
Taisen Deshimaru (1914–1982) was a figure in Buddhist and religious studies who studied under Kodo Sawaki (~1936–1965) and founded both the Association Zen Internationale and La Gendronnière.

Taishu Tagami is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University and earned a master's at the University of Tokyo. He served as a professor at Komazawa University (attested 1990) and concurrently lectured at the Eastern Institute (attested 1990).
Taishun Mibu is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at Taisho University until 1937 and later served there as director (attested 1972).

Taitetsu Unno (1929–2014) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied at UC Berkeley and the University of Tokyo (~1951–1968) and served as Jill Ker Conway Professor of Religion at Smith College (1971–1998).
